'''Othyus Jeffers''' (born August 5, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. Jeffers played [[college basketball]] with the [[UIC Flames|University of Illinois at Chicago]] for two years, before transferring to [[Robert Morris University (Illinois)|Robert Morris University]] for his senior season. He then started his professional career with the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]], a [[minor league]] basketball organization owned and run by the NBA. He has had stints with three prior NBA teams: the [[Utah Jazz]], the [[San Antonio Spurs]], and the [[Washington Wizards]]. He has also spent a short stint in [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italy]] with [[Pallacanestro Cantù|NGC Cantù]]. After his playing career, he returned to Robert Morris and served as head coach of the basketball team from 2017 to 2019.

==Early life==
Jeffers was born in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], to Geraldine Allen. He grew up in the Chicago's West Side. His three older brothers, Henry Allen, Gerome Allen and Edmund Allen, all played basketball in high school and Jeffers often attended his brothers' games and practice. In 1993, when Jeffers was in the third grade, Gerome was shot to death near the family's apartment. Nine years later, during his senior year at [[Hubbard High School (Illinois)|Hubbard High School]], he lost another brother. Edmund was shot to death in another shooting incident nearby. However, the incident did not stop him from playing basketball, as he and his half-brother and high school teammate, Standell King, attended practice just a day after the incident.<ref name="usatoday">{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2008-03-03-jeffers-naia-cover_N.htm|title=NAIA star knows dangers of playing close to home|first=Marlen|last=Garcia|date=March 4, 2008|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett Co, Inc|access-date=May 1, 2011}}</ref><ref name="saltlaketribune">{{cite web|url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/jazz/49530607-87/jeffers-jazz-nba-chicago.html.csp|title=Utah Jazz: For Jeffers, living life was hardest part of NBA dream |first=Ross|last=Siler|date=May 6, 2010|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|publisher=MediaNews Group|access-date=May 1, 2011}}</ref>

Prior to attending Hubbard, Jeffers attended and played basketball with [[Westinghouse Area Voc High School (Chicago, Illinois)|Westinghouse High School]]. He transferred to Hubbard as a sophomore and continued to play basketball there. He averaged 22 points and 11 rebounds per game as a junior. In his senior season, he led Hubbard to [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] Regional and Sectional titles while averaging 28 points and 16 rebounds per game. He graduated as the school's all-time leading rebounder with 1,987 rebounds.<ref name="uicflames">{{cite web|url=http://www.uicflames.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jeffers_othyus00.html|title=Othyus Jeffers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110106004405/http://www.uicflames.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jeffers_othyus00.html|work=UICFlames.com|publisher=CBS Interactive|archive-date=January 6, 2011|access-date=May 1, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==

===Community college and Illinois-Chicago===
Jeffers, who did not qualify academically for a [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] scholarship, opted to attend [[Los Angeles Southwest College]], a [[community college]] near the city of [[Los Angeles]]. He starred and averaged 22.3 points and 10.7 rebounds as a freshman. However, after a year, he returned home to Chicago and transferred to the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] (UIC). He reportedly rejected offers from [[Big East Conference|Big East]] and [[Big 12 Conference]] schools and chose to attend Illinois-Chicago in order to be close with his family who lived near the school. He started his college career with the [[UIC Flames]] in 2005, after sitting out the 2004–05 season while establishing academic eligibility.<ref name="uicflames"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/remaining_bios.pdf|title=Othyus Jeffers Bio|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=May 1, 2011}}</ref>

In the 2005–06 season, Jeffers played in all 31 games, 30 as a starter. He led the Flames in rebounding (7.6 rebounds per game) and assists (3.0 assists per game) and also ranked second in scoring with 11.6 points per game. He won the [[Horizon League]] Newcomer of The Year awards for his debut season with the Flames. He improved his performance in his junior season by averaging 15.4 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game in 32 games, all as a starter. He recorded a career-high 27 points and 14 rebounds at the [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|University of Pennsylvania]] on December 21, 2005. He led the team in both scoring and rebounding and was named in the All-Horizon League First Team. However, he had a difficult relationship and frequently clashed with head coach [[Jimmy Collins (basketball)|Jimmy Collins]].<ref name="usatoday"/><ref name="uicflames"/>

===Shooting incident===
A few weeks after his junior season finished, Jeffers was shot in the leg while trying to defend his sister from Andre Childs, his sister's boyfriend. His sister earlier called Jeffers for help in a dispute against Childs. Jeffers came to his sister's defense and confronted Childs. After a fight, Childs allegedly pulled a gun fired several shots. Two bullets hit both Jeffers and his sister. Jeffers was shot in the left thigh and his sister was hit in the left calf. Jeffers and his sister survived and Childs was later arrested and charged with attempted murder.<ref name="usatoday"/><ref name="saltlaketribune"/><ref name="deseretnews">{{cite web|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700014476/Utah-Jazz-A-dream-come-true-for-Othyus-Jeffers.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100307180533/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700014476/Utah-Jazz-A-dream-come-true-for-Othyus-Jeffers.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 7, 2010|title=Utah Jazz: A dream come true for Othyus Jeffers|first=Jody|last=Genessy|date=March 6, 2010|work=Deseret News|access-date=May 1, 2011}}</ref>

Jeffers was fortunate that the bullet went through his thigh without hitting any major arteries. He left the hospital that night after getting treatment, even though the doctor wanted him to stay overnight for further observation. Jeffers, who wanted to play basketball as soon as possible, was supposed to use crutches for three weeks but he only used them for three days. He then began to play basketball again in less than a month.<ref name="usatoday"/><ref name="saltlaketribune"/><ref name="deseretnews"/>

===Robert Morris University===
After the shooting incident, combined with his conflict with coach Collins, Jeffers transferred schools once again.<ref name="usatoday"/> He transferred to [[Robert Morris University (Illinois)|Robert Morris University]] who played in the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA). By transferring from an NCAA school to an NAIA school, Jeffers did not have to sit out another season. He also switched his major from psychology/sociology to business major. He concluded his college career there by averaging 24.0 points, 11.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game as a senior. He led the RMU Eagles to a [[Chicagoland Collegiate Athletic Conference]] (CCAC) championship and was named as the CCAC Player of the Year. He then played in the [[2007 NAIA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007 NAIA Basketball Tournament]], leading the Eagles to the Final Four, where they were defeated by the [[Concordia University (California)|Concordia University]]. Despite failing to win the championship, Jeffers was named as NAIA Player of the Year by [[Sporting News|The Sporting News]] and as co-Player of the Year the [[Basketball Times]].<ref name="jazz"/>

==Professional career==

===Iowa Energy (2008–09)===
Jeffers was [[Eligibility for the NBA Draft|automatically eligible]] for the [[2008 NBA draft]] after finishing his four-year college eligibility. However, he went [[Undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]]. He then signed a contract to play in the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League) and became eligible for the [[2008 NBA Development League Draft|2008 D-League draft]]. On November 7, 2008, Jeffers was selected 47th overall in the third round by the [[Iowa Energy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_board_08.html|title=2008 NBA D-League Draft Results|date=November 7, 2008|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105201943/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_board_08.html|archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> On February 11, 2009, after playing 24 games while averaging 19.9 points and 8.9 rebounds with the Energy, Jeffers was selected to the [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|D-League All-Star Game]] roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/allstar_replacements_090211.html|title=2009 NBA D-League All-Star Replacements Announced|date=February 11, 2009|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090319053548/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/allstar_replacements_090211.html|archive-date=March 19, 2009}}</ref> In the game, he scored 14 points as his team, the Red Team, defeated the Blue Team 113–103.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20090214/DLBDLR/recap.html|title=Sims And Ahearn Named Co-MVPs As Red Defeats Blue In All-Star Game|date=February 14, 2009|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He also participated in the [[NBA Development League All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|D-League Dream Factory Friday Night Slam Dunk Contest]], but was eliminated in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dream_factory_090213.html|title=James White Soars To NBA D-League Slam Dunk Championship|date=February 13, 2009|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He averaged 20.6 points on 53.5 percent shooting, 8.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game in 48 games and was named as the [[NBA Development League Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] for the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rookie_090410.html|title=Othyus Jeffers Named NBA D-League Rookie of the Year|date=April 10, 2009|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091218001622/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rookie_090410.html|archive-date=December 18, 2009}}</ref> He played one game in the D-League playoffs as the Energy was eliminated in the first round by the [[Dakota Wizards]]

===NGC Cantù (2009)===
During the offseason, he was selected to play with the NBA D-League Select Team in the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/select_team_090706.html|title=NBA D-League Select Team To Participate In NBA Summer League|date=July 6, 2009|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He played in two games, averaging 20.5 points and 7.0 rebounds in 23.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2009/statistics/index.jsp|title=2009 NBA Summer League Statistics|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> After failing to earn a spot in the NBA teams' training camp, he opted to play overseas with the [[Pallacanestro Cantù|NGC Cantù]] in [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italy]]. He left Cantù in December 2009 after only playing in 10 games while averaging 9.3 points and 5.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ansa.it/web/notizie/rubriche/altrisport/2009/12/28/visualizza_new.html_1649846908.html|title=Basket: Cantu'-Jeffers, e' addio|trans-title=Basketball: Cantu'-Jeffers, Goodbye|language=it|work=ANSA.it|publisher=Agenzia Nazionale Stampa Associata|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref>

===Second stint with Iowa Energy (2010)===
Jeffers returned to the D-League and rejoined the Iowa Energy on January 9, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_09-10.html|title=NBA Development League: 09–10 Transactions|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202102424/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_09-10.html|archive-date=December 2, 2010}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2010)===
On March 3, 2010, Jeffers was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Utah Jazz]]. Prior to the call-up, he was averaging 14.3 points and 6.8 rebounds per game in 22 games with the Energy.<ref name="jazz">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/030310_jazz_sign_othyus.html|title=Jazz Sign Othyus Jeffers to a 10-Day Contract|date=March 3, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He made his first NBA appearance on March 6, 2010, in a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He then signed a second 10-day contract on March 14, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/031410_jazz_sign_othyus.html|title=Jazz Signs Jeffers to Second 10-Day Contract|date=March 14, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> After playing in seven games for the Jazz, he was signed for the remainder of the season on March 24, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/032310_jazz_sign_othyus.html|title=Jazz sign Othyus Jeffers for the remainder 2009–10 season|date=March 24, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He played 10 games with the Jazz, averaging 2.6 points and 1.4 rebounds per game in 5.1 minutes per game. He also played 6 games in the playoffs.

===Third stint with Iowa Energy (2010–11)===
Jeffers remained on the Jazz roster throughout the [[2010 NBA Summer League]], the training camp and the preseason games. In the Summer League, he played in five games and averaged 7.6 points and 3.6 rebounds in 19.2 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2010/players/othyus_jeffers/|title=2010 NBA Summer League Statistics – Othyus Jeffers|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He then played in five preseason games, averaging 6.4 points and 2.4 rebounds in 8.6 minutes per game. However, he was waived before the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/roster/1011_jazzwaivefour_102110.html|title=Jazz Waives Four Players|date=October 21, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He then returned to the Iowa Energy for the [[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2010–11 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/returning_players_101030.html|title=2010 NBA D-League Returning, Affiliate, and Open Tryout Players|date=October 30, 2010|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104131507/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/returning_players_101030.html|archive-date=November 4, 2010}}</ref> On February 3, 2011, Jeffers, who was leading the league in scoring with 21.1 points per game, received his second selection to the D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/allstar_rosters_2011.html|title=2011 NBA D-League All-Star Rosters Announced|date=February 3, 2011|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> In the game, he scored 14 points as his team, the Eastern Conference All-Stars, defeated the Western Conference All-Stars 115–108.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20110219/ESTWST/gameinfo.html|title=Iowa's Courtney Sims Captures MVP Honors In 2011 NBA D-League All-Star Game|date=February 19, 2011|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110225163006/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20110219/ESTWST/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 25, 2011}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2011)===
After playing in 37 games and averaging 21.2 points on 48.0 percent shooting, 9.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game, Jeffers was called up to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He signed a 10-day contract with them on March 4, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_othyus_jeffers.html|title=Spurs Sign Othyus Jeffers To 10-Day Contract|date=March 4, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011}}</ref> He played only one game with the Spurs before he returned to the Energy on March 13.

===Washington Wizards (2011)===
Jeffers played one more game with the Energy before he was signed by the [[Washington Wizards]] on March 17, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/jeffers_031711.html|title=Wizards Sign Othyus Jeffers|date=March 17, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011}}</ref> He signed his second 10-day contracts with the Wizards on March 27, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/jeffers_032711.html|title=Wizards Sign Jeffers to Second 10-Day Contract|date=March 27, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011}}</ref> On April 6, 2011, he was finally signed for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/owensjeffers_040611.html|title=Wizards Sign Jeffers and Owens for Remainder of Season|date=April 6, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 27, 2011}}</ref> He scored 15 points, in a game against the [[Miami Heat]] on March 20, 2011, his first double-figure scoring game in the NBA. Two days later, he started his first NBA game in a game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He recorded his first [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] with 13 points and 11 rebounds on April 9, 2011. He played 16 games with the Wizards, averaging 5.7 points and 4.1 rebounds per game in 13.0 minutes per game. Although he ended the season with the Wizards in the NBA, Jeffers was named to the [[All-NBA Development League Team|All NBA D-League Second Team]] and the [[NBA Development League All-Defensive Team|NBA D-League All-Defensive First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/alldleague_2011.html|title=NBA D-League Announces 2010–11 All-League Selections|date=April 13, 2011|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111108215718/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/alldleague_2011.html|archive-date=November 8, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/johnson_110416.html|title=Dakota's Chris Johnson Named NBA D-League Defensive Player of the Year|date=April 16, 2011|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=April 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110221420/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/johnson_110416.html|archive-date=November 10, 2012}}</ref>

After the 2010–11 season, Jeffers became a [[Free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]] as the Wizards extended a qualifying offer to him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-pick-up-rookie-options-extend-qualifying-offer-to-nick-young-but-not-yi-jianlian/2011/06/18/AG4M8daH_blog.html|title=Wizards pick up rookie options, extend qualifying offer to Nick Young but not Yi Jianlian|date=June 18, 2011|first=Michael|last=Lee|publisher=The Washington Post|work=Wizards Insider|access-date=September 28, 2013}}</ref> However, the [[2011 NBA lockout]] prevented him from signing the qualifying offer. He also suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn anterior cruciate ligament]] in his right knee during a workout in July and was ruled out for six to eight months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-othyus-jeffers-recovering-from-torn-acl/2011/10/30/gIQA1HYyXM_blog.html|title=Wizards' Othyus Jeffers recovering from torn ACL|date=October 31, 2011|first=Michael|last=Lee|publisher=The Washington Post|work=Wizards Insider|access-date=September 28, 2013}}</ref> The Wizards subsequently withdrew the qualifying offer, thus making him an unrestricted free agent. Jeffers went on to miss the entire 2011–12 season.

===Fourth stint with Iowa Energy (2012–14)===
In September 2012, Jeffers was invited to the [[Phoenix Suns]]' training camp and preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/20121001othyus-jeffers-undeterred-despite-long-odds.html|title=Othyus Jeffers undeterred despite long odds|date=October 1, 2012|first=Paul|last=Coro|publisher=The Arizona Republic|work=azcentral sports|access-date=September 28, 2013}}</ref> He played in one preseason game before he was waived by the Suns before the 2012–13 regular season started.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/20121015phoenix-suns-waive-othyus-jeffers-more-cuts-come.html|title=Phoenix Suns waive Othyus Jeffers; more cuts to come|date=October 15, 2012|first=Paul|last=Coro|publisher=The Arizona Republic|work=azcentral sports|access-date=September 28, 2013}}</ref>

He returned to the D-League and rejoined the Iowa Energy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html|title=Full List of 2012 Returning, Affiliate and Local Tryout Players Invited to NBA D-League Training Camps|date=October 31, 2012|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=September 28, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218094230/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html|archive-date=December 18, 2015}}</ref> He averaged 14.7 points on 48.6 percent shooting, 5.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game in 33 games. At the end of the season, Jeffers was named to the NBA D-League All-Defensive Third Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_development_league_announces_all_nbadleague_selections_2013_04_26.html|title=NBA Development League Announces 2012–13 All-NBA D-League Selections|date=April 26, 2013|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com/DLeague|access-date=September 28, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427213213/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_development_league_announces_all_nbadleague_selections_2013_04_26.html|archive-date=April 27, 2013}}</ref>

Jeffers joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. He played in six games, averaging 8.2 points and 3.8 rebounds in 15.5 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2013/players/sl_othyus_jeffers/|title=2013 Summer League Statistics|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 13, 2013}}</ref> On September 26, 2013, he signed with the Timberwolves for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-brown-hummel-and-jeffers-camp-roster|title=Wolves Sign Brown, Hummel And Jeffers To Camp Roster|date=September 26, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 13, 2013}}</ref> He was later waived by the Timberwolves on October 25.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-waive-brown-jeffers Wolves Release Lorenzo Brown and Othyus Jeffers]</ref>

In November 2013, he was re-acquired by the Iowa Energy.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/20132014_energy_training_camp_2013_11_04.html 2013–2014 Energy Training Camp Roster]</ref> On January 24, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs sign Othyus Jeffers|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140124_spurs_sign_jeffers|access-date=January 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2014}}</ref> On February 1, 2014, he was waived by the Spurs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs Sign Shannon Brown to 10-day Contract; Release Othyus Jeffers|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140201_spurs_sign_shannon_brown|access-date=February 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2014}}</ref>

On February 3, 2014, Jeffers was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=2014-02-07 }}</ref> On February 6, 2014, he re-joined the Iowa Energy.

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014)===
On April 8, 2014, Jeffers signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-othyus-jeffers Wolves Sign Othyus Jeffers]</ref>

On April 24, 2014, Jeffers and [[Ron Howard (basketball)|Ron Howard]] were named the co-MVPs of the NBA D-League for the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/ron_howard_othyus_jeffers_nba_dleague_MVP_2014_04_24.html Ron Howard and Othyus Jeffers Named 2014 NBA D-League Co-MVPs] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429161113/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/ron_howard_othyus_jeffers_nba_dleague_MVP_2014_04_24.html |date=2014-04-29 }}</ref>

===Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters (2014)===
On May 4, 2014, he signed with the [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]] for the 2014 PBA Governors’ Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/talk-n-text-taps-nba-d-league-mvp-othyus-jeffers-for-governors-cup |title=Talk ‘N Text taps NBA D-League MVP Othyus Jeffers for Governors’ Cup |access-date=May 5, 2014 |archive-date=May 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506163534/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/talk-n-text-taps-nba-d-league-mvp-othyus-jeffers-for-governors-cup |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his one and only appearance for Talk 'N Text on May 21 as he recorded 38 points, 13 rebounds and 2 steals in the 105–99 win over [[Meralco Bolts]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Philippines/2014/0521_1693_2348.asp Regular Season Round 2: Meralco Bolts – Talk N Text 99–105]</ref>

Jeffers did not play in the 2014–15 basketball season reportedly because of a knee injury he suffered.

===Barangay Ginebra San Miguel (2016)===
On January 4, 2016, he signed with the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel]] for the [[2016 PBA Commissioner's Cup]] and also for the [[2016 PBA Governors' Cup|2016 Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{ cite news |last=Dy |first=Richard |title=Cone taps NBA D-League MVP as Ginebra import |url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/2016/01/05/1539526/cone-taps-nba-d-league-mvp-ginebra-import |work=[[The Philippine Star]] |location=[[Manila]] |date=January 5, 2016 |access-date=January 30, 2016 }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On December 22, 2016, it was announced that Jeffers would return to [[Robert Morris University (Illinois)|Robert Morris University]] of the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA) and served as associate head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Head Men's Basketball Coach Al Bruehl to Retire Following 2016–2017 Season; Former Eagle Othyus Jeffers Named Successor|url=https://www.rmueagles.com/article/2163|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630012616/https://www.rmueagles.com/article/2163|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 30, 2020|date=December 22, 2016|website=rmueagles.com|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> He accumulated a 9–19 record during his first season as head coach in 2017–18.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moore to play men's basketball at Robert Morris |url=https://gomcpanthers.com/news/2018/5/24/moore-to-play-mens-basketball-at-robert-morris.aspx |website=Morton College |access-date=July 16, 2023 |date=May 24, 2018}}</ref>
